reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the first three premises regarding impurity-driven segregation and softening in a Ti-V-Nb-Ta RHEA, but it provides no specific evidence for the fourth premise that spark plasma sintering with gettering will achieve the necessary impurity reduction in a Ti-Ni-based HEA.
premises: Trace interstitial oxygen and nitrogen promote nanoscale phase segregation and precipitate-free zones (PFZs) during elevated-temperature aging in refractory high-entropy alloys.
This impurity-induced segregation depletes the matrix of solute interstitials, causing progressive softening (loss of solid-solution strengthening) with aging time.
Better control of impurities is needed to improve the stability of RHEAs for high-temperature applications.
Spark plasma sintering under ultra-high purity conditions can significantly reduce oxygen and nitrogen incorporation compared to conventional processing.
